document_summary: Chapter 158 of the City of Hoboken, NJ Code, covering mandatory disclosures for rent increases over 10% (Ord. B-750) and a prohibition on algorithmic rent fixing (Ord. B-781).

rules.title: Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
rules.requirement: Residential landlords raising rent by more than 10% year over year on a lease renewal must give the existing tenant specified disclosures before the increase takes effect. These are an itemization of the costs, a statement on whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the tenant's right to take legal action, and Division of Housing contact information.
rules.key_value: Disclosures required for renewal rent increases of more than 10% (no cap on the increase itself)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords increasing rent by more than 10% upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant, year over year
rules.interaction: This is a disclosure rule, not a rent cap. It also requires a statement on whether a rent algorithm was used, which links it to the algorithmic rent-fixing ban in § 158-2.
rules.quoted_span: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year shall be required to make the following disclosures to existing tenants either in the lease upon renewal (must be clearly indicated on the first page) or on a form provided by the Hoboken Division of Housing prior to the increase being implemented:
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Classified under rent_increase_limits as an increase-notice requirement, although it sets no cap. Penalty (fine up to $1,000 per incident) omitted from key_value.

rules.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords of residential dwelling units in Hoboken may not price-fix using algorithmic pricing. That means using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information in order to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors.
rules.key_value: Ban on price fixing using algorithmic pricing (software or data-sharing platforms using nonpublic competitor information)
rules.coverage_conditions: Any residential dwelling unit, defined as any primary residence, in the City of Hoboken. 'Nonpublic competitor information' is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost.
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from 'residential dwelling unit'.
rules.interaction: Possible preemption by New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) once it takes effect. The FAIR Act is not addressed in this document.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: NJ's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) may preempt Hoboken's algorithmic-rent ordinance once it takes effect. Not found in this capture.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Enforcement is by the Division of Housing or aggrieved private citizens in Hoboken Municipal Court. Penalties (up to $2,000 fine, up to 90 days community service, or N.J.S.A. 40:49-5 penalties) are omitted from key_value.
